name: Rachika Nayar
label: NNA Tapes
lede: She started on guitar at ten, rescored an anime at 20-something as Rachika S, then processed her playing into ambient records that suddenly had a trance kick drum under them.

eras.title: Rachika S, scoring other people's pictures
eras.text: Nayar grew up in State College, Pennsylvania, where both parents were Penn State professors, and picked up guitar at ten. Before her own albums she was a Brooklyn DIY musician making soundtracks for films that already existed or were about to.

years.h: Early days in Brooklyn DIY, including the queercore band Mallrat
years.p: Before her solo records, Nayar played in the Brooklyn DIY scene, including a queercore band called Mallrat, according to Paste.
years.xp: Paste's Best of What's Next profile lists Mallrat among the projects she worked on around the scene. She has also described making synth-pop with close friends in high school and drum and bass breakdowns in Ableton, so the guitar-and-laptop hybrid came from a wide pile of habits.

years.h: Themes For A Film: Rachika S rescores Tekkonkinkreet
years.p: Her first release, on Brooklyn's Loveless Records, swaps the anime's soundtrack for nine instrumentals of her own, from ambient to downtempo to techno.
years.xp: Loveless lists the tracklist as nine pieces, from the 1:23 opener "Intro // The Fire" to the 5:47 "Killing Machines" and the closer "A House By The Ocean". She was releasing under the name Rachika S at the time, and dropped the initial when her full-length albums arrived.

years.h: She scores the feature film So Pretty
years.p: Wikipedia credits her with the soundtrack, and Magnetic Magazine lists film scoring among her work before her first album.

eras.title: Four years of guitar loops become an album
eras.text: Our Hands Against the Dusk took four years to finish and arrived on NNA Tapes in March 2021. Its companion EP followed on RVNG Intl. five months later.

years.cap: Our Hands Against the Dusk, NNA Tapes, 2021
years.h: Our Hands Against the Dusk: four years in the making
years.p: Her debut LP on NNA Tapes layers processed guitar with strings, piano and a Korg M1 synth.
years.xp:
Nayar told Magnetic Magazine she leaned on the Korg M1's vocal patches, which she called "angelic and very haunting". Ricky of YATTA sang on "Losing Too Is Still Ours", and she then pitch-shifted and time-stretched the vocal. Zeelie Brown played cello on the closer, "No Future".

Her touchstones, per the same interview, were Brian Eno's take on "Canon in D" and Hiroshi Yoshimura's Wet Land. Paste says the collaboration with Yatta Zoker on "Losing Too Is Still Ours" is what led to the album.

years.big: I like when electronic music feels organic.
years.h: Why the guitar never sounds like a guitar for long
years.p: Nayar's method, as she described it to SLUG Magazine: record loops, then put them through a prism of processing until one idea comes out as many.
years.xp: She told SLUG that playing an instrument and producing on a computer each felt like "only singular facets" of her emotional life, so she uses both. The same interview ties her interest in transformation to queer experience and to rave culture's shared-but-solitary feeling.

years.h: fragments: the raw loops behind the album
years.p: An EP of guitar etudes on RVNG Intl.'s Commend imprint, serving as companions to Our Hands Against the Dusk.
years.xp: Fragments was the stripped version of her process: the improvised guitar loops that she normally buries under synths and strings. It was reissued in April 2023 with seven extra tracks, a story that picks up in the last era.

eras.title: Trance drums, Maria BC and a Pitchfork No. 29
eras.text: Her second LP added club pulse and vocals to the guitar ambience. It became her biggest record so far, and a year-end fixture.

yt: Official video: Heaven Come Crashing (feat. Maria BC)
years.h: Title track with [[Maria BC|24e8a36c-85f1-45ee-8ae4-35b49cef8d60]] is the first single
years.p: Maria BC sings on the title track, which BrooklynVegan called widescreen electro-pop, and again on "Our Wretched Fate".
years.xp: Nayar told The FADER she found Maria BC through the song "Good Before". Adding vocals was new territory for her.

years.src: Album of The Year · Stereogum · The FADER · Wikipedia · BrooklynVegan
years.h: Heaven Come Crashing lands: Pitchfork gives it 8.4
years.p: Pitchfork named it Best New Music and ranked it No. 29 of 2022, after Stereogum made it Album of the Week.
years.xp:
Albumoftheyear.org lists Pitchfork's score as 84, which is 8.4 out of 10. Nayar wrote, produced and mixed the record herself, with extra mixing by Carlos Hernandez and mastering at Black Knoll Studio. Stereogum's James Rettig called the range "sinister, playful, traumatic, ecstatic" and put it at No. 35 on its own year-end list.

Unlike the debut, most of the songs were finished in six months to a year, she told The FADER: she felt clearer about her tools. The album draws on electronic film soundtracks and trance-club aesthetics, and her aim, she said, was for music to overwhelm the listener.

years.h: Cafe Oto in London, then the Glad Cafe in Glasgow
years.p: The release tour opened with summer festivals in Portugal, Czechia, Finland and Canada, then Cafe Oto on September 12 and Glasgow the next night.
years.xp: BrooklynVegan's tour list also has Fremont Abbey in Seattle on July 29, Public Records in Brooklyn on October 1, Sleeping Village in Chicago on October 6 and 2220 in Los Angeles on October 8.

yt: Heaven Come Crashing (The Sight Below Remix)
years.h: The Sight Below remixes the title track
years.p: Ambient producer The Sight Below took the title song into a remix, one of the album's follow-ups.

eras.title: Expanded, reissued, paired up
eras.text: After the album came the back catalog getting its due, and a collaborative record.

years.p: RVNG Intl. put out an 18-song fragments on vinyl, and NNA Tapes reissued Our Hands Against the Dusk on vinyl the same day.
years.xp: The FADER said "hawthorn" is a slow build that dissipates without release. It also noted that Heaven Come Crashing made its own list of the 50 best albums of 2022.

years.p: A collaboration with Nina Keith, released on Smugglers Way.
